consensus_summary: The seal/mark in the forehead is the sign of divine ownership, identification, protection from judgment, and allegiance of God's faithful people (forehead signifying mind/loyalty), commonly linked to the name of God and/or the Holy Spirit, in deliberate contrast to the mark of the beast.
book_summary: The Name impressed upon its owner, marking covenant identity and allegiance in the forehead; God's seal joins ownership with departure from iniquity, while the counterfeit claims the same place.
consensus_core_identification: Divine ownership/identification/protection/allegiance mark on the faithful (often via God's name).
book_core_identification: The Name impressed, marking covenant identity and allegiance (ownership joined to departure from iniquity).
rationale: Minimum cores are equivalent: both identify the forehead seal as God's Name/ownership mark of covenant identity and allegiance on His people (with the standard antithesis to the beast's mark). Book's phrasing ('The Name impressed... joins ownership with departure from iniquity') restates elements already present in the consensus primary readings and bases (Rev name-in-forehead texts + 2 Tim 2:19), without altering referent, excluding consensus cases, or introducing contradiction. Extra details (high-priest plate, etc.) are immaterial wording/precision, not a change of extension or core.
strongest_objection: Consensus sometimes foregrounds the Holy Spirit as the sealing agent more than the bare 'Name,' so a reader could claim the book slightly narrows the mechanism; yet the Name is already inside the consensus primary and does not replace it.
